title: 第一次挂科之后
title_en: After My First Failed Exam: An Email to My Sister
summary_zh: Lin 统计学考试没过，第一个告诉的是姐姐。她在邮件里冷静地分析了原因：笔记看了无数遍，题却一道没自己做过，并给自己定了补考计划。读完你会学到 I wish I had… 和 If I could…, I would… 的用法。
body: Hi Mei, I have some bad news, and I'm telling you first because you won't panic. I failed my statistics exam. I got the result this morning, and I've been walking around campus ever since, trying to work out what went wrong. Honestly, I already know the answer. I read my notes again and again, but I never practised a single problem on my own. In the exam, I recognised every question and still couldn't solve most of them. I wish I had your patience with numbers, but wishing won't help, so I've made a plan. There's a resit at the end of the summer, and I'm going to do two practice problems every day instead of rereading. I've also booked a meeting with my tutor to go through my paper. If I could go back to the start of term, I would ask for help in the first week, not the last. Please don't tell Mum and Dad yet. I'd rather tell them myself once I have a plan that works. Could you call me this weekend? If you had half an hour, you could test me on the basics. Love, Lin

questions.prompt: What does Lin think was the real reason she failed?
options: She did not have enough time to read her notes
She read her notes but never practised solving problems
The exam questions were completely new to her
Her tutor did not explain the topics clearly
questions.evidence: I read my notes again and again, but I never practised a single problem on my own.

questions.prompt: Why doesn't Lin want Mei to tell their parents yet?
options: She thinks their parents will blame Mei
She hopes to pass the resit before they find out
She wants to tell them herself when she has a working plan
She has already asked her tutor to contact them
questions.evidence: I'd rather tell them myself once I have a plan that works.

questions.prompt: Why does Lin tell Mei the news first?
options: Mei failed the same exam
Mei is her tutor
Mei will tell their parents for her
She thinks Mei will stay calm
questions.evidence: I'm telling you first because you won't panic

questions.prompt: What does "resit" mean in "There's a resit at the end of the summer"?
options: a summer holiday
a second chance to take an exam
a new class
a piece of homework
questions.evidence: There's a resit at the end of the summer

vocabulary.example: Don't panic if you can't answer the first question.
I recognised her voice before I saw her face.
If you miss the exam, you can take the resit in August.
Learning a language takes a lot of patience.
Before you try the hard questions, make sure you know the basics.

expressions.note: 复盘失败时的常用说法：Let's look at what went wrong. 语气客观，不带指责。
强调重复，常带“没什么效果”的意味。
on one's own = by oneself，强调没有别人帮忙。
go through 指仔细检查、逐项讲解：Let's go through the answers together.
I'd rather + 动词原形，表达个人偏好，比 I want to 更委婉。
test sb on sth：请朋友帮忙抽查复习内容时很实用。

knowledge.quote: I wish I had your patience with numbers
knowledge.explanation: I wish + 过去式 had，表示“希望现在拥有”但事实上没有，是与现在事实相反的愿望。注意这里 had 是“有”，不是过去完成时。

knowledge.quote: If you had half an hour, you could test me on the basics.
knowledge.explanation: if + 过去式，主句用 could + 动词原形，提出一个假设性的、很客气的请求。比 Can you test me? 更委婉，给对方留了余地。

knowledge.quote: I've also booked a meeting with my tutor to go through my paper.
knowledge.explanation: to go through my paper 是不定式表目的，说明“约见导师是为了什么”。相当于 in order to go through…，但更简洁自然。

speaking: 用 1 分钟讲一次你没考好的经历：原因是什么？下次你打算怎么做？用上 I wish I had… 和 If I could…, I would…。
writing: 用 120–150 词给一位家人写邮件，告诉他/她一件不太好的消息，并说明你的应对计划。至少用一个不定式表目的，并用上 what went wrong。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 I wish I had… 说一个你希望自己现在就具备的能力或品质。
task.model: I wish I had your patience with numbers

title: 给同学当小老师
title_en: Explain It to Me: A Peer Tutoring Session
summary_zh: Ella 卡在一道物理题上，学霸 Ravi 却不直接给答案，而是让她用自己的话把题目讲一遍。讲着讲着，她自己就想通了。读完你会学到辅导同学时很好用的几句口语。
body: Ella: Thanks for doing this, Ravi, because I've been staring at question four for an hour. Ravi: No problem, so what's confusing you? Ella: Everything, to be honest: neither the lecture slides nor the textbook explains why the answer is negative. Ravi: Okay, forget the answer for now and explain the question to me in your own words. Ella: You want me to explain it to you? You're the one who got top marks. Ravi: Trust me, it helps, because talking it through shows us exactly where you get stuck. Ella: Fine, so a ball is thrown straight up, and we need its velocity after two seconds. Ravi: And what's happening to it during those two seconds? Ella: It's going up, but it's slowing down the whole time — oh, wait! Ravi: Keep going. Ella: So by two seconds it has already stopped and started to fall, and that's why the answer is negative! Ravi: Exactly, and the minus sign just shows the direction. Ella: But why didn't you just tell me that? Ravi: Because you'd have forgotten it by Friday. You worked it out yourself, so it'll stay with you. And honestly, explaining things helps me remember them too.

questions.prompt: Why does Ravi ask Ella to explain the question herself?
options: He has forgotten how to solve the problem
He wants to check whether the textbook is wrong
He believes she will understand and remember it better
He is too tired to explain it again
questions.evidence: You worked it out yourself, so it'll stay with you.

questions.prompt: What does Ella realise about the ball?
options: It has already started falling after two seconds
It keeps going up faster and faster
It stops completely and never comes down
It moves in the same direction all the time
questions.evidence: So by two seconds it has already stopped and started to fall

questions.prompt: Why does Ravi say "you'd have forgotten it by Friday"?
options: Ravi will be away on Friday
Answers you are simply told are easy to forget
The exam is on Friday
Ella has a very bad memory
questions.evidence: You worked it out yourself, so it'll stay with you.

questions.prompt: What does "velocity" mean in "we need its velocity after two seconds"?
options: speed in a particular direction
weight
colour
height
questions.evidence: we need its velocity after two seconds

vocabulary.example: The instructions were so confusing that nobody finished the task.
If you take ten from five, the result is negative.
We walked in the wrong direction for twenty minutes.
I always get stuck on the last question.

expressions.note: 放在句首或句尾，引出坦白的想法，语气比 honestly 稍正式一点。
老师常说 Explain it in your own words.，检验是否真懂，而不是背原文。
劝对方接受自己的做法，口语中很常见，带一点“我有经验”的意思。

expressions.meaning: 把它从头到尾说一遍；一起理一理
expressions.note: talk sth through：通过讨论把问题理清楚，也可说 talk me through it。
鼓励对方沿着思路往下走，辅导、教练时常用。

expressions.meaning: 让你记住；留在你脑子里
expressions.note: sth stays with sb：某事让人长久记得，The story stayed with me for days.

knowledge.quote: neither the lecture slides nor the textbook explains why the answer is negative
knowledge.explanation: neither A nor B 作主语时，谓语和离它最近的 B 保持一致：the textbook 是单数，所以用 explains，虽然前面的 slides 是复数。

knowledge.quote: You want me to explain it to you?
knowledge.explanation: want sb to do sth：想让某人做某事。不定式 to explain 前面的 me 是动作的执行者，不能说 want that I explain。

knowledge.quote: talking it through shows us exactly where you get stuck
knowledge.explanation: 动名词短语 talking it through 作 because 从句的主语，把一个动作当成一件事来说，所以谓语用单数 shows。

speaking: 和同伴模拟：一人扮演卡在难题上的同学，一人当小老师。用 1 分钟引导对方自己想出答案，用上 in your own words 和 Keep going。
writing: 用 100–130 词写一段你给别人讲题（或别人给你讲题）的经历，说明讲解为什么有帮助。至少用一个动名词作主语的句子。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 neither… nor… + 单数动词 说一件让你困惑的事。
task.model: neither the lecture slides nor the textbook explains why the answer is negative

title: 选修课怎么选才不后悔
title_en: Four Questions to Ask Before You Pick an Elective
summary_zh: 选修课是课表里唯一能完全自己做主的部分，可很多人只是跟着朋友选。这篇指南给出四个问题帮你判断一门课值不值得选。读完你会学到 it's worth doing、leave room for 等实用表达。
body: Electives are the only part of your timetable that you get to choose freely, so it's worth thinking carefully before you click. Here are four questions to ask yourself. First, would you still take this class if none of your friends were taking it? Choosing a course just to stay with your group often means a whole term of boredom. Second, what could this class give you that your main subject can't? A history student might learn more from a basic coding course than from yet another history module. Third, have you read the course description properly? Look for the way students are assessed. A class marked entirely on one final exam feels very different from one built around weekly projects. Fourth, can you talk to someone who has already taken it? Second-year students are usually happy to tell you whether the reading list is manageable. Finally, leave a little room for curiosity. Some of the best classes are the ones people choose almost by accident, simply because the title made them smile.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the guide?
options: To help students think carefully about which electives to take
To persuade students to choose coding instead of history
To explain how universities mark final exams
To warn students never to take classes with friends
questions.evidence: Here are four questions to ask yourself.

questions.prompt: In the guide, what does "manageable" suggest about a reading list?
options: It is very interesting to read
It is not too much to deal with
It is chosen by the students themselves
It is only used for the final exam
questions.evidence: whether the reading list is manageable

questions.prompt: Why does the writer mention a history student taking a coding course?
options: To say that history is boring
Because coding is a required subject
Because history students are bad at coding
To show that an elective can give skills your main subject cannot
questions.evidence: what could this class give you that your main subject can't?

questions.prompt: Who does the writer suggest talking to before choosing?
options: The head of the university
A first-year student
Your parents
Someone who has already taken the class
questions.evidence: can you talk to someone who has already taken it?

vocabulary.example: My timetable is full on Mondays but empty on Fridays.
He started drawing in his notebook out of boredom.
This course is assessed by two essays and a presentation.

vocabulary.meaning: 可以应付的；不算太多的
vocabulary.example: If you break the project into small steps, it feels much more manageable.
She opened the box out of curiosity.

expressions.note: it's worth + 动名词：表示某事值得花时间去做，It's worth checking twice.
给建议时常用，引导读者自我反思：Ask yourself what you really want.
a whole + 时间 + of + 名词，强调持续时间长，带一点夸张。
yet another 带“又来了”的语气，暗示数量已经很多：yet another meeting。
leave room for sth：计划里留出余地，leave room for dessert / mistakes。
by accident 表示“不是计划好的”，almost 让语气更自然。

knowledge.quote: would you still take this class if none of your friends were taking it?
knowledge.explanation: 主句用 would + 动词原形，if 从句用过去进行时 were taking，提出一个与现在情况不同的假设，帮读者检验自己的真实动机。

knowledge.quote: Here are four questions to ask yourself.
knowledge.explanation: 不定式 to ask yourself 放在名词 questions 后面作定语，表示“要问的问题”。类似：a book to read, something to eat。

knowledge.quote: A class marked entirely on one final exam feels very different from one built around weekly projects.
knowledge.explanation: marked… 和 built… 是过去分词短语，放在名词后作定语，表示被动：“完全按期末考试打分的课”“围绕每周项目设计的课”。

speaking: 用 1 分钟向学弟学妹推荐（或劝退）一门你上过的选修课。用上一个 would…if… 的问句和 it's worth…。
writing: 用 120–150 词写一篇“选课建议”，给出三条理由或提醒。至少用一个过去分词作定语（如 a class marked…），并用上 leave room for。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 Would you still… if…? 写一个问题，帮朋友检验他做某个决定的真正原因。
task.model: would you still take this class if none of your friends were taking it?

title: 一边上学一边打工
title_en: Fixing Bikes Between Lectures: A Student with a Part-Time Job
summary_zh: Daniel 因为一个瘪了的车胎，在校门口的自行车店找到了兼职。他聊了怎么兼顾打工和学习、这份工作最好和最难的部分。读完你会学到 swap shifts、a student first 等实用说法。
body: Interviewer: Daniel, you work at the bike repair shop near the main gate. How did that start? Daniel: I came in with a flat tyre in my first month, and the owner was so busy that I offered to help. By the end of the week, he'd offered me a job. Interviewer: How many hours do you work? Daniel: Two evenings a week and Saturday mornings. Interviewer: Is it hard to balance work and study? Daniel: Sometimes. During exam weeks, either my boss or my classmates have to be patient with me. Usually I swap shifts with another student working there, and that saves me. Interviewer: What's the best part of the job? Daniel: Honestly, the people. Students come in looking stressed because they're late for class, and twenty minutes later they ride off smiling. Interviewer: And the worst part? Daniel: I wish I had more free evenings. My friends go to the cinema on Thursdays, and I'm usually covered in oil at that time. Interviewer: Would you recommend a part-time job to other students? Daniel: Yes, but only if it's flexible. Find a boss who understands that you're a student first.

questions.prompt: What does Daniel enjoy most about his job?
options: Earning money to go to the cinema
Learning how to repair expensive bikes
Seeing worried customers leave happy
Working with his classmates on Saturdays
questions.evidence: and twenty minutes later they ride off smiling

questions.prompt: How does Daniel usually manage during exam weeks?
options: He stops working until the exams are over
He swaps shifts with another student
He studies in the shop when it is quiet
He asks the owner to close the shop early
questions.evidence: Usually I swap shifts with another student working there

questions.prompt: What is the interview mainly about?
options: Why students should not have jobs
A student's experience of a part-time job at a bike shop
How to repair a flat tyre
A shop owner's business plan
questions.evidence: you work at the bike repair shop near the main gate

questions.prompt: What does "flexible" mean in "only if it's flexible"?
options: easy
well paid
able to change to suit your needs
close to home

vocabulary.example: It will cost a lot to repair the old car.
Thank you for being so patient with me.
I always feel stressed in the week before exams.
My working hours are flexible, so I can leave early on Fridays.

expressions.note: 英式拼写 tyre，美式 tire；get a flat tyre = 爆胎/轮胎没气。
offer to do sth 是主动提出做某事；offer sb sth 是给某人提供东西（如 offered me a job）。
balance A and B：在两件事之间找到平衡，也常说 work-life balance。
和同事临时调换上班时间：Can we swap shifts on Friday?
be covered in + 名词：身上沾满某物，covered in mud / paint。
X first 强调身份的优先级：I'm a parent first and a manager second.

knowledge.quote: Students come in looking stressed because they're late for class, and twenty minutes later they ride off smiling.
knowledge.explanation: looking stressed 和 smiling 是现在分词作伴随状语，描述学生“进来时”和“离开时”的状态，比再加一个从句更生动简洁。

knowledge.quote: I wish I had more free evenings.
knowledge.explanation: I wish + 过去式 had，表达对现在情况的遗憾：事实是他现在晚上没什么空。说现在的愿望用过去式，说过去的遗憾才用 had done。

knowledge.quote: either my boss or my classmates have to be patient with me
knowledge.explanation: either A or B 作主语时，谓语与离它最近的 B 一致：my classmates 是复数，所以用 have to，而不是 has to。

speaking: 用 1 分钟说说：你觉得大学生该不该做兼职？用上 I wish I had… 和 balance work and study。
writing: 用 120–160 词写一段你做过（或想做）的兼职经历：怎么找到的、最好和最难的部分。至少用一个现在分词作伴随状语。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 …come in looking…, and… later… 描写一个人前后的变化。
task.model: Students come in looking stressed because they're late for class, and twenty minutes later they ride off smiling.
